summary: Client CDN prefetch leads to residency header mismatch and APAC p95 latency spike
description:
Issue summary: KoiHealth reported a sudden increase in client-observed p95 latency for requests from APAC customers. They observed that a subset of requests were routed to US edge egress, which increased TLS handshake and RTT and caused p95 to jump from ~160ms to ~620ms. Customer believes their browser or CDN prefetch behavior is causing residency headers to be cached incorrectly and triggering control-plane selection of a non-local egress.

Impact: Elevated p95 for production inference traffic for KoiHealth across APAC region for ~20% of requests; user-facing slowdowns and some request timeouts at mobile-device scale. No token billing discrepancies reported.

Environment: prod:apac-southeast (customer tenant id: koi-9981). Traffic originates from mobile clients using a CDN vendor (FastEdge) plus browser prefetch enabled in their app.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) App opens on APAC mobile client with CDN prefetch enabled.
2) Prefetch requests to our /v1/chat endpoint occur on app background/idle.
3) Subsequent interactive request is sent shortly after; client observes X-Redwood-Residency header set to "apac-southeast" but control plane routes egress to us-east-1 for ~1 in 5 requests.
4) Observed p95 spikes on client traces and TLS handshake delays in our edge logs.

Observed logs/metrics:
- edge-proxy logs (apac-southeast) show upstream egress selection: egress=us-east-1 on ~18% of active sessions in the 03/12 08:00-10:00 window.
- auth logs show token-scoped residencies are present and unexpired.
- TLS handshake histogram: p95 increased from 160ms -> 620ms for affected session IDs.
- Control-plane decision traces show a cache hit for token->residency mapping but a miss for client-ip->edge affinity; fallback policy selected remote egress.

Initial customer impact: degraded UX for end users in APAC during morning peak; customers are requesting mitigation (prefer strict residency enforcement or short TTL changes).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: client-side CDN prefetch created persistent connections or cached DNS entries that caused the edge-proxy to see source IPs or SNI hints that mapped to a different region. Alternate hypothesis: FastEdge is doing prerouting on behalf of the client and reusing a US egress POP causing the control plane to observe inconsistent client-origin metadata.

What we checked so far:
- Correlated request IDs from customer traces to our edge traces; confirmed that the same client token was used and residency metadata was present.
- Verified token residency mapping in control plane: token residency = apac-southeast, TTL healthy.
- Edge proxy behavior: sticky-session table shows entries with last_seen from FastEdge IP ranges; these entries map to us-east-1 egress due to FastEdge ASN->geo mapping returning US in some cases.
- DNS evidence: FastEdge appears to pre-resolve our public edge hostname and then reuse a cached socket to a US POP for subsequent requests.

Next steps:
- Request FastEdge logs from KoiHealth (done, awaiting).
- Add temporary control-plane override to treat CDN-prerouted x-forwarded-for as non-authoritative for residency decisions for KoiHealth token scope (can be toggled per-tenant). Needs review from Network/Infra.
- Instrument edge proxy to log fastedge-asn and socket-reuse flags for a 6h window.
- Consider recommending customer disable CDN prefetch for critical auth-bound calls as a short-term mitigation.

workaround: If customer disables CDN prefetch for auth-bound endpoints in their mobile SDK, observed incidence drops to <1%. Recommended as immediate short-term workaround while we validate tenant override.
